title: Addressing multiple facets of ligand-receptor network inference including single-cell proteomics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the paper's only new dataset, GSE309679 (human gene counts, 1.4 MB gzipped): 60,675 gene rows x 13 sample columns (11 pancreatic-cancer patient-derived xenograft models plus 2 control tissues), confirmed by NCBI esummary (n_samples=13). Also downloaded the reference ligand-receptor table LRdb_122019.txt from the companion GitHub repository: 3,251 rows, 3,239 unique ligand-receptor gene-symbol pairs, all of them positives, columns ligand/receptor/names/source/PMIDs. Listed the full companion repository tree (only R analysis scripts plus reference databases; no feature/label table).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The single-cell proteomics example (SCoPE2 mass-spectrometry data on U-937 cells: 3,042 proteins in 1,490 cells, 122 ligands and 89 receptors after mapping to gene symbols) and the two reused transcriptomics sets (GSE228415 CD40L-CD40 single-cell RNA-seq; GSE59831 FACS-sorted mouse lung bulk RNA-seq) were read in the Methods; I did not download them because no label column exists to pair them with. The Europe PMC supplementary-file listing timed out and was not retrieved.

a1_downloadable.note: GSE309679 counts downloaded openly from the NCBI GEO FTP site; LRdb and all analysis scripts downloaded from GitHub/Zenodo. No login or access application anywhere.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no outcome column anywhere in these files. The quantity of interest - whether a ligand-receptor pair is genuinely active between two cell populations - has no measured ground truth in this paper or in the field (the LIANA+ benchmark says so explicitly), so the label would have to be constructed by running an inference tool or by inventing a spatial proxy. Verified in the files: the counts matrix holds only read counts, and LRdb holds only curated positive pairs with no activity or context column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present as values, not references: raw gene-level read counts with Ensembl identifiers and HUGO symbols in the counts file; gene symbols in LRdb (protein sequences would need a UniProt lookup, but that is one bulk mapping, not thousands of manual steps).

a4_units_stated.note: Counts file columns are plainly integer sequencing read counts per gene per sample (verified by eye: values 0-1,920 in the first rows); the Methods state STAR alignment against GRCm39/human and that read counts came from STAR.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL for the paper's own new data: GSE309679 is 13 bulk RNA-seq samples (the modelling unit is the sample/xenograft, not the gene), far under the ~1,500-row bar. The reused single-cell proteomics example has 1,490 cells but only two cell states, and 3,239 LRdb pairs are all positives from a 2019 third-party compilation.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything I opened totals well under 100 MB: 1.4 MB gzipped counts, 1.1 MB LRdb, ~70 MB of reference network/pathway text files. Comfortable on a 16 GB laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Matches: the paper describes a collection of pancreatic-cancer xenografts plus two controls, and GEO/the file both give 13 samples. The proteomics figures quoted in the text (3,042 proteins, 1,490 cells) are from the cited SCoPE2 paper and were not independently checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL. The only thing resembling a label is the tool's own ligand-receptor interaction score (a regularised correlation/expression product computed from the same expression values that would be the features). That is leakage by construction plus circularity: any model trained on it distils SingleCellSignalR rather than learning biology, and its ceiling is that tool's unvalidated accuracy.

existing_models.name: SingleCellSignalR V2 (this paper's own software, an R/Bioconductor package that scores ligand-receptor interactions from single-cell data)
existing_models.score_and_split: No predictive accuracy reported on any held-out split; the paper is a framework description with illustrative case studies and no ground-truth evaluation.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The authors state that tools disagree markedly, that performance is dataset-dependent, and that no universal ligand-receptor tool can be established - i.e. they name the absence of ground truth as the open problem.

existing_models.name: LIANA+ (an all-in-one framework collecting and comparing cell-cell communication scoring methods)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reports AUROC, balanced accuracy and normalised F1 against an indirect proxy truth built from spatial co-localisation (Moran's R > 0, false-discovery rate < 0.05) on five slide-tags single-nucleus RNA-seq datasets; no real measured labels.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: States that systematic benchmarks are still pending and evaluation remains limited by the lack of ground truth.

existing_models.name: CellChat (Nature Communications 2021, a network- and law-of-mass-action-based cell-cell communication inference method)
existing_models.score_and_split: No supervised accuracy number; validated by agreement with known signalling biology in case studies.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Absence of a gold standard for which interactions are truly active.

existing_models.name: Dimitrov et al. 2022 (Nature Communications) comparison of cell-cell communication methods and resources
existing_models.score_and_split: Showed low agreement between tools and strong dependence on the chosen ligand-receptor resource; concordance, not accuracy, because no truth set exists.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Named the lack of a ground-truth benchmark as the field's central obstacle.

existing_models.name: CellComNet and PriorCCI (ensemble and interpretable deep-learning classifiers of ligand-receptor interactions from single-cell transcriptomes, 2023-2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Report classification metrics, but their positive labels come from curated ligand-receptor databases and their negatives are randomly sampled pairs - the same constructed-label problem.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell foundation models) would be the natural backbone for expression input, with ESM-2 (a protein language model) for ligand/receptor sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU-only laptop would suffice for embedding 3,239 ligand-receptor pairs with a small ESM-2 checkpoint
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; scGPT and Geneformer are open but Geneformer carries use restrictions. Irrelevant here because there is nothing to fit a head to.

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt plus AlphaFold DB (for ligand/receptor sequence and structure) or spatial transcriptomics atlases (as a co-localisation proxy)
integration.join_key: Gene symbol mapped to UniProt accession, or Ensembl gene identifier (ENSG, present in the counts file)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could sequence and structure of a ligand-receptor pair predict whether it is actually active in a given tissue context - unanswerable here because no dataset in this paper records whether any pair was active.

controls.positive_control: Known CD40L-CD40 signalling in the GSE228415 dataset, which the paper itself uses as a sanity check, is the one real positive control available.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable in principle, but with no real label there is nothing meaningful to shuffle.
controls.external_validation: None with measured labels; the field substitutes spatial co-localisation proxies, which are themselves model assumptions.

honest_claim_h3: The most a model built on these files could honestly claim is that it reproduces SingleCellSignalR's own interaction scores on expression data it was not trained on - a statement about one tool's behaviour, not about which ligand-receptor interactions are real.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene and protein expression to predict which ligand-receptor pairs are actually signalling between two cell populations.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell-population expression of a ligand gene and its receptor gene, from single-cell RNA sequencing or mass-spectrometry proteomics. I verified only 13 bulk samples of new data here; the reused proteomics example has 1,490 cells but just two cell states.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the pair is genuinely active between those populations. The true answer would have to come from a direct experiment (blocking antibody, receptor knockout, spatial proximity), and no such measurement exists in this paper or, by the field's own admission, in any public benchmark.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer and immunology labs pick drug targets from these predictions, so a validated version would matter a great deal - but without measured labels the project can only mimic an existing unvalidated tool.

more_or_better_data.why: The paper's own new data is 13 bulk RNA-seq samples (verified in the downloaded counts file). Everything else it analyses is reused from other papers: GSE228415, GSE59831 and the SCoPE2 proteomics of 1,490 cells. LIANA+ and the Dimitrov benchmark already span far more datasets.

confidence_score.why: There are no replicate measurements of interaction activity to calibrate against, because activity is never measured. The existing tools already attach permutation-based p-values, which is as far as the data allows.

models_beatable.why: Not because the tools are strong, but because nobody can be beaten: LIANA+ (2024), CellChat (2021) and this paper all evaluate without ground truth, so there is no number to beat. 'Beating' would just mean agreeing differently with another unvalidated tool.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The condition that fails is the most basic one: there is no shared label measuring the same quantity the same way, so no split and no added data can guarantee improvement over the existing baselines.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: train a model to predict active ligand-receptor interactions between cell populations from single-cell expression (transcript and protein), using this paper's framework output as the label. Dead because the label is the tool's own score computed from the same expression values that would serve as features, and because the paper's new data is 13 bulk samples. The alternative - sequence-based prediction of ligand-receptor pairing from the 3,239 LRdb pairs - also fails, since LRdb is positives-only, borrowed from FANTOM5/HPMR/HPRD in 2019, and negatives would have to be invented.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes I actually downloaded (1.4 MB gzipped counts, 1.1 MB LRdb, ~70 MB reference text files); nothing was timed because no modelling task survived Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows of the paper's own deposited data and look for an outcome column: 13 samples, 60,675 genes, no activity label. That one command kills it.

verdict_reason: Software/framework paper with no label to predict. A2 and A8 both fail: whether a ligand-receptor interaction is active is never measured, so the only candidate label is the paper's own tool score computed from the same expression values that would be the features (circular and leaky by construction). A5 fails too - the only new data deposited is 13 bulk RNA-seq samples (verified in the downloaded file), and the reused single-cell proteomics example covers just two cell states. The field itself (LIANA+, Dimitrov et al.) states the ground truth does not exist.
